title: How to Find Good Tradesmen and Keep Them
meta_description: How to find good tradesmen for your construction business: define what you actually need, widen where you look, vet properly, and use referrals well.
h1: How to Find Good Tradesmen and Keep Them
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to hiring trades you can put in front of a client without worrying.

intro.answer: Finding good tradesmen is a process, not luck. Most bad hires trace back to a vague brief: if you cannot describe the work and the standard precisely, you cannot judge who is right for it.

image.alt: A skilled construction team working together on site

intro.roadmap: This guide covers five steps: defining what you need, widening where you look, vetting properly before anyone starts, knowing when to trust your instincts, and using referrals so good people bring you more good people.

briefing.title: Define the Job Before You Look
briefing.intro: Almost every hiring problem in construction starts before the search does. A brief that says experienced carpenter tells you nothing you can vet against, so the decision falls back to whoever seemed keenest on the phone.

panels.heading: What should you decide before you start looking?
paragraphs: The project scope in plain terms: what is being built, to what standard, and what finished looks like. Then the skills that scope actually demands, rather than a job title.
Then the practical constraints. Timeline, budget, and where the work is. Those three decide who is genuinely available to you, and they save both sides a conversation that was never going to work.

panels.heading: Then work through it in order
paragraphs: Each step narrows the field. Skipping one means the next has to do work it was not designed for.
steps: Define the need: scope, skills, timeline, budget, location.
Cast a wide net rather than reusing the same two sources every time.
Vet thoroughly, before anyone is on site rather than after.
Trust your instincts. If something feels wrong at interview, it usually is.
Ask for referrals, because good tradesmen tend to know other good tradesmen.

review.label: Worth remembering
review.text: Vetting after someone has started is not vetting, it is damage control. The cost of a bad hire is rarely their day rate. It is the rework, the delay and the client who watched it happen.

heading_rewrites.3. Conduct Thorough Vetting: Essential S: 3. How should you vet a tradesman?

append_sections.heading: Write a Brief That Can Be Judged Against
append_sections.before_heading: 5. How to Find Good Tradesmen: The Power of Referrals
paragraphs: Start by writing a brief that sets out the project specifics: measurements, architect plans, materials, finishes, and any fixtures or fittings you have in mind. That is what lets a tradesperson understand what you actually expect rather than guess at it.

Then be precise about qualifications. Some trades have no formal entry requirements while others need specific certifications: gas engineers must be Gas Safe registered, and electricians usually need Part P certification for domestic work. Getting this wrong is the kind of mistake that surfaces at inspection.

Think about experience too. Time served is a reasonable indicator of skill. Ask how long someone has been in the trade and get them to explain their approach to the job, because how they describe the work tells you more than how long they have done it.

append_sections.heading: Evaluate the Soft Skills, Not Just the Trade
append_sections.before_heading: 5. How to Find Good Tradesmen: The Power of Referrals
paragraphs: Technical ability is the entry requirement. Communication, teamwork and problem solving decide whether someone is worth putting in front of a client, and a LinkedIn study found that 92% of professionals rate soft skills as equally or more important than technical ones.

Assess them by watching how candidates behave in the interview itself. Look for clear communication, active listening and adaptability. Ask about working in teams and handling conflict, and put a realistic scenario to them to see how they would approach it.

append_sections.heading: Screen With a Structure
append_sections.before_heading: 5. How to Find Good Tradesmen: The Power of Referrals
paragraphs: Review CVs properly, looking for relevant experience and qualifications rather than scanning for a trade name. Plan the questions in advance, focusing on what they have actually achieved and why they left previous roles.

Then run the interview the same way every time. Open warmly, ask the candidate to talk through their experience, and listen closely, because the detail is where the useful information sits. Include behavioural questions so you are hearing about real situations rather than intentions.
